newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan union warns government against inaction.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan union warns government against inaction.

text.p: Union leaders of Venezuela's public sector workers, on strike for more than a week, warned the government on Friday to satisfy their pay demands or risk an escalation of the labour dispute.
Thousands of civil servants have been on strike for 10 days in protest over delays in paying salary bonuses in the worst labour dispute of President Rafael Caldera's term.

Carlos Borges, president of the Federation of Public Sector Workers warned that if the bonuses were not received by Monday, "the conflicts will grow, union actions will be reinforced and things could get out of control."
Caldera and his ministers have assured unions that the bonuses will be paid but Borges insisted that workers would not return to work until they had received their money.

Caldera's government is facing an increasing number of year-end protests and strikes as the effects of a deep economic crisis cut into living standards. Public sector workers earn an average of $106 per month.
